name: ping
justification: The original supplied transport must retain ping readiness.

name: dsu-empty
justification: There are no vertices or operations, hence no output states.

name: dsu-singleton
justification: Both operations are self-unions of the only singleton.

name: dsu-merges-and-repeats
justification: Three disjoint pairs form first; merging two gives size 4, then merging the final pair gives size 6; duplicate and self-unions change nothing.

name: kruskal-empty
justification: An empty graph has the empty forest and no components.

name: kruskal-isolates
justification: All four vertices are isolated components; no edge may be chosen.

name: kruskal-loops-parallels-negative
justification: Components are {0,1,2}, {3,4}, {5}. In the triangle the two cheapest connecting edges cost -2 and 0; component {3,4} costs -1. Loops cannot enter a forest; edge 7 is an equally valid substitute for edge 5.

name: kruskal-ties
justification: Any two distinct triangle edges connect its three vertices at cost 2; vertex 3 is isolated.

name: kruskal-64bit-positive
justification: The input is a tree, so every edge is required: 4*10^9 exceeds signed 32-bit range.

name: kruskal-only-loops
justification: Even a very negative loop cannot connect distinct vertices; all vertices remain isolates.

name: prim-empty
justification: An empty graph has the empty forest and no components.

name: prim-isolates
justification: All four vertices are isolated components; no edge may be chosen.

name: prim-loops-parallels-negative
justification: Components are {0,1,2}, {3,4}, {5}. In the triangle the two cheapest connecting edges cost -2 and 0; component {3,4} costs -1. Loops cannot enter a forest; edge 7 is an equally valid substitute for edge 5.

name: prim-ties
justification: Any two distinct triangle edges connect its three vertices at cost 2; vertex 3 is isolated.

name: prim-64bit-positive
justification: The input is a tree, so every edge is required: 4*10^9 exceeds signed 32-bit range.

name: prim-only-loops
justification: Even a very negative loop cannot connect distinct vertices; all vertices remain isolates.

name: scc-empty
justification: Both arrays are empty for the empty directed graph.

name: scc-isolates
justification: No distinct vertices are mutually reachable.

name: scc-one-component
justification: The 0-1-2 cycle and two-way 2-3 connection make every vertex mutually reachable; the loop adds no condensation edge.

name: scc-condensation-dedup
justification: Mutually reachable sets are {0,1}, {2,3}, {4}, {5}, {6}. Three input edges from the first SCC to the second become exactly one pair; the self-loop is internal.

name: scc-reverse-chain
justification: Each vertex is its own SCC: no reverse reachability exists. Labels are arbitrary and are compared by partition, not exact integer.

name: topo-empty
justification: The empty order is a valid permutation of zero vertices.

name: topo-isolates
justification: Any permutation is valid because there are no precedence edges.

name: topo-diamond-and-duplicates
justification: Vertex 0 precedes 1 and 2, both precede 3; a duplicate edge does not create a directed cycle.

name: topo-edge-to-finished
justification: The edges imply 0<2<1. Under natural adjacency order, edge 2->1 reaches an already finished vertex, which is not a cycle.

name: topo-self-loop
justification: A self-loop is a directed cycle even in an otherwise empty component.

name: topo-disconnected-cycle
justification: The separate 3-4-3 cycle invalidates the whole graph, including vertices outside the first DFS tree.

name: topo-three-cycle
justification: Following the three edges returns to the active starting vertex.

name: dag-singleton
justification: The only reachable route is the zero-edge route from the source to itself.

name: dag-isolates-source-two
justification: Only source 2 is reachable. Unreachable distances must be null, and every parent is -1.

name: dag-negative-route
justification: Route 0-1-2 costs -4, beating direct cost 8; appending 2->3 gives cost 0. Vertex 4 is unreachable.

name: dag-finite-minus-one
justification: Distance -1 to vertex 1 is finite and must not be confused with unreachable vertex 2.

name: dag-tied-parallel
justification: Two parallel edges reach 1 at cost 2, and two routes reach 3 at cost 3. Any correct original incoming edge IDs are accepted.

name: dag-nonzero-source-and-incoming
justification: Source 3 reaches 0 by two tied routes of cost -1. Vertex 4 is unreachable despite its incoming edge to the source; source keeps distance 0 and parent -1.

name: dag-64bit-negative
justification: The unique route to vertex i has i edges of weight -10^9; final distances exceed the negative 32-bit range.

name: dag-64bit-positive
justification: The unique route to vertex i has i edges of weight 10^9; final distances exceed the positive 32-bit range.

name: dag-unreachable-negative-component
justification: No edge leaves the source component toward vertices 2,3,4, so their negative edges must never be relaxed.

name: dag-unreachable-cycle
justification: Vertices 3 and 4 form a directed cycle unreachable from 0; a global cycle check must still reject the graph.

name: dag-self-loop
justification: The reachable self-loop makes the graph non-DAG; no distance or parent array may be returned.

name: dag-unreachable-self-loop
justification: An unreachable zero-weight self-loop is still a global cycle.
